extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news publishers, media researchers, and platform/policy observers
extracted.subtask_short: curation of Apple News Top Stories
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of how Apple News UK editors select items for the human-curated Top Stories section, and the effects of those selection practices on publishers, audiences, and the product. Focuses on selection patterns, format requirements, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source diversity in Top Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Over three-quarters of articles chosen for the human-curated Top Stories section of Apple News UK come from six major publishers (77 percent combined); three outlets (Sky News, BBC News, Evening Standard) consistently accounted for over half of all recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concentration indicates limited exposure to a broad range of publishers and implies a failure to surface diverse voices; reviewers should measure diversity by share of unique publishers featured and repeat-rate of top outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favoring major mainstream outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple News UK’s Top Stories appear to prioritize big mainstream outlets: two major broadcasters (BBC News and Sky News) accounted for around 40 percent of featured articles, and commentators report smaller sites feel the app favors large players.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether editorial selection is skewed toward well-known brands rather than quality or topical relevance from smaller outlets; consider presence/absence of medium and small publishers in featured slots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to use Apple News Format (ANF)
rubrics_metrics.description: To stand a chance of being included in Top Stories, publishers must use Apple News’ native, proprietary file format (ANF) rather than directing readers back to their own websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion eligibility is effectively constrained by technical format adoption; evaluations should account for whether selection is of 'best coverage' overall or only of coverage published in ANF, and note which outlets publish in ANF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial trade-off for publishers publishing in ANF
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple’s proprietary format generates minimal revenue for publishers; publishers are often asked to give away content for traffic exposure, forcing a trade-off between traffic and direct revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing fairness or sustainability, examine the economic incentives and whether participation requires publishers to sacrifice monetization (e.g., direct site visits, ad revenue) in exchange for Apple-driven traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection rationale: context, explanation, and thoughtfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple’s editors (per press accounts) select stories that provide context, explanation, or thoughtful nuance—pieces described as providing 'the most context and explanation on why the news mattered' or 'nuanced' coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging story merit, consider depth, explanatory power, and nuance as positive selection attributes; compare selected pieces against alternatives that may be click-driven but less explanatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unequal access to editorial channels (pitching advantage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some major publications reportedly have direct access to Apple News editors through dedicated Slack channels, allowing them to pitch stories—an advantage not available to all publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate process fairness by documenting which publishers have direct pitching channels and whether such access correlates with higher placement rates in Top Stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of transparency about selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple has disclosed few details about how and why it selects certain publishers for inclusion in featured sections; reasons for frequent promotion of specific outlets remain unclear and Apple did not respond to requests for comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit selection processes for transparency: availability of public criteria, explanations for choices, and responsiveness to inquiries. Transparency deficits hamper accountability and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence and audience impact of Top Stories placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Top Stories is among the most prominent parts of Apple News (first section displayed and present in Today View widget); being featured drives significant traffic spikes—e.g., Bloomberg saw a 400 percent spike linked to Top Stories inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the downstream impact of placement (traffic, referral spikes, audience growth) and treat Top Stories inclusion as a high-stakes editorial decision with material effects for publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-design effects that limit editorial choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple’s combination of proprietary format (ANF) and insufficient monetization creates a situation where editors can only choose from a restricted pool of willing publishers, hamstringing the depth and quality of the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider systemic constraints (technical, economic) that shape editorial selection; assess whether curatorial claims (human editors as antidote to algorithmic problems) are undermined by product design choices that narrow the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension between human curation claims and elitism critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple positions human editors as differentiating the product from algorithmic rivals by prioritizing reputation and news value, but critics argue the practice remains 'elitist' and tends to favor established outlets over broader representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether human curation meaningfully improves content quality vs replicating existing power structures; check for patterns that show preferential treatment of established brands despite the stated editorial mission.
